description.value: The study investigated the neural and structural bases of processing costs associated with ambiguous doubly-quantified sentence comprehension using BOLD fMRI in healthy young adults and volumetric MRI in bvFTD patients and healthy seniors.

spans.text: In the present study, we investigated the neuroanatomic basis for the resolution of doubly-quantified sentence meaning in two experiments.

description.value: The study comprised an fMRI experiment in healthy young adults and a behavioral and volumetric MRI experiment in bvFTD patients and healthy seniors.

value: A whole-brain analysis of doubly-quantified sentences relative to unambiguous baseline sentences revealed activation of five cortical regions, including peri-Sylvian regions in left IFC and left plTC, as well as left dlPFC, right rostral PFC, left inferior parietal cortex, and dorsomedial PFC. These findings indicate that additional brain regions beyond peri-Sylvian cortex are recruited during processing of ambiguous sentences.

spans.text: A whole-brain analysis of doubly-quantified sentences relative to unambiguous baseline sentences revealed activation of five cortical regions (see Figure  3  and Table  2 ). This included peri-Sylvian regions in left IFC and left plTC. We additionally observed activation beyond peri-Sylvian cortex that extended from left IFC into left dlPFC and also included other clusters in right rostral PFC (rPFC), left inferior parietal cortex, and dorsomedial PFC.
